The round was led by LMnT Ventures, with participation from Regeneration VC, Humba Ventures, and Massive Technology Ventures\. # A new medical AI study found the same flaw in OpenEvidence, OpenAI, Anthropic, and Doximity \| Fortune OpenEvidence, founded in 2021, is a free, ad-supported AI search engine for doctors that pulls answers straight from peer-reviewed medical journals at the point of care and labels how strong the evidence is\. It’s become somewhat of the poster child of the medical AI boom\. In February, a Sequoia-led round valued the company at $1 billion\. In the following months, that number grew to $3\.5 billion by July with GV and Kleiner Perkins co-leading, $6 billion in October to $12 billion this January, in a round co-led by Thrive Capital and DST Global\. That’s roughly $700 million raised in about a year\. Meanwhile, competitor Doximity has taken an enterprise approach\. Best known as a professional networking platform for physicians, it now sells an AI assistant called Ask that helps doctors summarize patient notes, check drug interactions, and draft documentation\. Ask is folded into paid, enterprise contracts with more than 150 health systems\. Every answer runs through a human-review layer called PeerCheck, where physicians check AI output against the original sources it’s citing\.

# Clarity Systems Secures $4\.4 Million Clarity Systems, an AI powered company that can detect retail fraud by seeing inside returned products without having to open them, said it has just closed a $4\.4 million seed round\. In a statement, it said the funding was backed by LMnT Ventures, with participation from Regeneration VC, Humba Ventures, and Massive Technology Ventures\. Clarity System said its technology sees inside returned and received products in three seconds without having to manually open them, which allows retailers to catch counterfeits, product swaps, and manipulation by comparing items or potential fraudulent items against the original manufacturer profile\. It’s similar to how an airport X-ray scanner identifies the contents of luggage without unpacking it\. Clarity’s system analyzes the product, and instantly detects anomalies such as counterfeit goods, product swaps, missing components, or other forms of return fraud\. # Tanvi leads strong women's show, Srikanth crashes out in mixed day for India at Korea Masters India’s Tanvi Sharma\. Third seed Tanvi, who recently clinched her maiden BWF World Tour title at the Taipei Open, eased past China's Yuan An Qi 21-16, 21-15 to progress to the second round\. Rakshitha Ramraj recovered from a game down to beat Korea's Yoo A Yeon 22-24, 21-12, 21-13, while Mansi Singh fought back to defeat Kim Joo Eun 14-21, 21-19, 21-9\.
